notes.13: Although most candidates correctly identified the movement of molecules in liquids and solids, there were a few who thought that there was no movement of the molecules in a solid.
notes.15: Most candidates understood that liquid Y, with the larger expansivity, expands more than liquid X, which has the smaller expansivity. However, some candidates did not realise that liquid Y contracts more than liquid X when it is cooled.
notes.16: Only stronger candidates were able to identify the materials from which the pan was made and showed good practical understanding of conduction. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics November 2021
notes.21: Only stronger candidates showed an understanding of total internal refraction. The question clearly stated that the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle and therefore, all the light is reflected back into the glass.
notes.28: This question proved challenging for many candidates. The circuit is a form of potentiometer, the current is the same in both resistors and therefore (using V = I R ) the potential difference across the 2.0 Ω is twice that across the 1.0 Ω resistor. The total potential difference across the two resistors is the sum of the potential differences across the two resistors which is 18 V.
notes.29: Most candidates recognised that the energy lost is in the form of low-grade thermal energy.
notes.31: The majority of candidates correctly identified the components in the circuit. Those who got it wrong, almost always confused cells with batteries.
notes.32: Many candidates thought that the total resistance of two resistors in parallel is equal to the average of the two resistances rather than it being smaller than either resistor. The logic is that the charge carriers now have a choice of paths to take, meaning that more charge carriers can pass per unit time.
notes.33: Only stronger candidates showed full understanding of the role of the earth wire in a domestic electricity supply.
notes.37: Only stronger candidates demonstrated their understanding of the α -scattering experiment. To show full understanding of the experiment, candidates needed to know that a small proportion of the α -particles are repelled by the nucleus and that the electric charge on the nucleus is produced by the protons in the nucleus.
notes.39: Candidates were expected to be able to identify the types of radiation in an absorption experiment from the results of the experiment. To do this, they needed to show knowledge of penetration of the different types of radiation through different materials. Only stronger candidates showed this basic knowledge.
notes.40: Only stronger candidates answered this correctly. Candidates needed to be familiar with, and to fully understand the meaning of half-life in order to answer this type of question. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics November 2021
